newsitem.title: UK: Britain cautious about international gold talks.
newsitem.headline: Britain cautious about international gold talks.

text.p: Britain gave guarded support on Tuesday to a conference of all countries that handled Nazi gold during World War Two to discuss compensation for Holocaust survivors.
"We are open to the idea of a conference, but we would want to ensure that it has a clear purpose and was properly prepared," a Foreign Office statement said.
Two British members of parliament and a colleague from the European Parliament on Monday won the backing of Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti for a conference when they met him in Zurich.
The leader of the delegation was Labour legislator Greville Janner, a vice-president of the World Jewish Congress and a critic of Swiss wartime gold purchases from Hitler's Germany.

Janner wants to get international agreement that $68 million of gold seized by the allies at the end of the war and still in the vaults of the British and American central banks be used to compensate Holocaust survivors and their families.
"We need to have a clearer idea from Mr Janner exactly what role he foresees for a conference," the Foreign Office said.

But it said Britain supported in principle the idea of benefitting individual victims of Nazism when the gold, administered by a Tripartite Gold Commission (TGC) which also includes France, is distributed.
"We are discussing this with the French and US governments, and with Jewish groups," it said.

British diplomatic sources have said the U.S., Britain and France agreed two weeks ago not to distribute the gold they still hold until they establish whether it could be given to Holocaust survivors.

The gold is all that remains of 377 tonnes -- now worth $4.1 billion -- recovered at the end of World War Two by Allied forces. The rest has already been distributed by the TGC to ransacked central banks.
Switzerland paid the Allies 250 million Swiss francs under a 1946 agreement to repay about half of its war-end stock of Nazi German gold worth 500 million Swiss francs at the time.
In 1946, the dollar was worth 4.30 Swiss francs.
